newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Solana praises NATO troops in Bosnia.
newsitem.headline: Solana praises NATO troops in Bosnia.

text.p: NATO Secretary-Gernal Javier Solana on Thursday praised NATO troops in Bosnia for the "professionalism and dedication" with which they had attempted to detain two indicted war criminals in Prijebor in Bosnia.
"We will not tolerate any behaviour by any of the parties contrary to the Dayton peace agreement," he said in a statement.
The statement said NATO-led SFOR troops had returned fire "in self defence" after one of the indicted men fired at them after being challenged.

The statement underlined that the troops' actions were undertaken under the SFOR (Stabilisation Force) mandate which allows troops in Bosnia to detain indicted war criminals when encountered in the course of their duties.

The statement made no reference to individuals but in Sarajevo NATO said war crimes suspect Simo Drljaca, who was police chief in the northwestern town of Prijedor until last autumn, had been shot dead after opening fire on troops who tried to detain him.
The troops had also detained another suspect, Milan Kovacevic, director of a hospital in Prijedor, without incident in a separate operation, NATO said.
